subject: Necessary to keep seperable effects for time/space in non-seperable space-time models?

messages.author: 79c3f1d031d4b461
messages.subject: Necessary to keep seperable effects for time/space in non-seperable space-time models?
parts:
Hello everyone, I'm still new to INLA, and therefore I set my models up, on what I consider best practice from books etc. And adapt from there for my needs.


In Blangiardo and Cameletti's "Spatial and Spatio-temporal Bayesian Models with R" (2015) they explain non-separable space-time models with Knorr Held Type interactions of type I-IV (chapter 7.2.1, p. 240). For example:


formula.intIV<- y ~ f(ID.area,model="bym",graph=Georgia.adj) +
    f(ID.year,model="rw2") +
    f(ID.year1,model="iid") +
    f(ID.area.int,model="besag", graph=Georgia.adj, group=ID.year.int, control.group=list(model="rw2"))


They explain themselves that Knorr Held interactions of type II assumes an autoregressive structure on time. So I was wondering, what's the conceptual reason for keeping extra effects (random and auto-correlated) for time, in all of the example?

When I played around with such interactions (but with an SPDE, not with a "bym" model) I noticed that dropping those extra effect for time did not change the DIC or WAIC.


So my question is: should one in general still keep the separable time-effects, despite using a spatial-temporal effect? When would it (not) be advisable? How about the separable spatial term?


Best,
Vincent
